title: Entanglement-enhanced fluctuation-free daemonic ergotropy with random measurements
authors: Saptarshi Roy, Pritam Halder, Tamal Guha, Hyunseok Jeong
abstract: Optimized daemonic ergotropy can make entanglement thermodynamically dispensable in measurement-assisted work extraction: for a fixed system marginal, quantum-classical states can reproduce the maximal work obtainable by optimizing the auxiliary measurement. We show that this equivalence is broken when the auxiliary measurement is randomized. For qudit-qubit quantum-classical states under Haar-random projective measurements, we derive upper bounds on the averaged daemonic gain and prove a gain-fluctuation trade-off, showing that any positive randomized gain necessarily entails measurement-induced fluctuations. In sharp contrast, a family of two-qubit entangled pure states attains the algebraic maximum of the gain allowed by a system marginal while remaining fluctuation-free for every measurement basis, yielding at least twice the gain achievable by any quantum-classical state with the same marginal. We further demonstrate that such conclusion holds when general two-qubit separable states are considered positioning randomized gain as a sufficient criterion for entanglement certification. Finally, we show that the entanglement advantage persists under partially randomized measurements sampled from a polar cap around the optimal basis. These results establish randomized daemonic ergotropy as a thermodynamic probe of entanglement and exhibit the connection between measurement-induced work fluctuations on the type of correlations: quantum entanglement vs classical.
summary: This work develops the concept of randomized daemonic ergotropy to quantify the thermodynamic advantage provided by quantum entanglement. It proves that while optimal measurements might not reveal an advantage, randomizing the measurement process exposes a fundamental trade-off: achieving positive average gain requires non-zero fluctuations for classical states, whereas entangled states can maintain high gain while remaining fluctuation-free.
main_problem: The paper investigates the role of quantum entanglement in enhancing work extraction (ergotropy) when the assisting measurement is randomized, defining this as randomized daemonic ergotropy (RDE). It aims to establish RDE as a thermodynamic probe for entanglement.
main_result: When measurements are randomized, the advantage of entanglement over classical correlations becomes apparent: entangled states can achieve higher average gain while remaining fluctuation-free, a feat impossible for quantum-classical states.
method: The analysis involves deriving upper and lower bounds on the randomized gain and fluctuation using mathematical techniques, comparing performance under optimal versus Haar-random measurements.
model_or_system: The model uses bipartite quantum systems ($ho_{SA}$) undergoing work extraction via projective measurements on an auxiliary system (A). The analysis focuses on two-qubit systems and the comparison between entangled and separable states.
key_observables: Randomized Daemonic Ergotropy Gain ($\Delta E_{ho SA}^D$), Fluctuation ($F_{ho SA}^D$), and standard Ergotropy ($	ext{Erg}(ho_S)$).
important_parameters: The degree of entanglement, the measurement basis randomness (Haar measure), and the fixed system marginal ($ho_S$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mathematical properties of ergotropy, convexity arguments, and the assumption of random projective measurements.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically contrasts the RDE extraction process, showing the performance gap between entangled and classically correlated states under randomized measurements.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the benchmark of optimal measurements, then introducing the randomized setting, deriving bounds on gain and fluctuation for quantum-classical states, and finally demonstrating the entanglement advantage using specific entangled states and deriving necessary conditions for fluctuation-free gain.
why_interesting: The connection between measurement-induced work fluctuations and the type of quantum correlation (entanglement vs. classical) provides a novel, measurable thermodynamic signature for entanglement, which is highly relevant to open quantum systems theory.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the randomized daemonic ergotropy (RDE) extraction process. Random measurements on the auxiliary system A assist ergotropy extraction from the system S, and the extracted ergotropy is averaged over the measurement ensemble. In contrast to the conventional setting with optimized assisting measurements, randomized measurements reveal a clear separation between the per- formance of (a) entangled states and (b) classically correlated states. Entanglement can provide both a larger average ergotropic gain and reduced measurement-induced fluctuations.

FIG. 2. Randomized daemonic gain with fixed system marginal ρS = p |0⟩⟨0|+(1−p) |1⟩⟨1|. The maximal value of gain in RDE, ob- tained from general separable states via Theorem 5 is plotted against p (solid blue line). The linear bound for the cq states obtained in Theorem 1 is plotted via dashed orange lines. The green solid line is the maximal achievable gain for optimal pure entangled state (Corol- lary 1). All axes are dimensionless.
